title: Mortgaging Your Land Title for a Bank Loan: Rights and Risks
desc: Mortgaging a house and land for a bank loan: notarisation, whether you can still live in, lease or sell, when the bank can enforce, and how proceeds are split.
summary: What borrowers should know when mortgaging a house and land to a bank under the 2015 Civil Code and the Land Law 2024: the mortgagor's rights and duties and how the asset is dealt with if the loan cannot be repaid.
body: p

Mortgaging a land use right certificate (sổ đỏ) to borrow money for building, buying a home or running a business is very common. Understanding your rights and obligations as a mortgagor helps you stay in control and avoid losing your home through avoidable oversights.
h2
1. What is a mortgage? Is the house on the land mortgaged too?
p

A mortgage means using an asset you own to secure the performance of an obligation without handing the asset over to the mortgagee; the mortgagor keeps the asset (Article 317 of the Civil Code). The borrower continues to live in the house; usually only the title documents are held by the bank, as agreed.
ul
If a land use right is mortgaged and the house on the land also belongs to the mortgagor, the house is also mortgaged property, unless otherwise agreed (Clause 3, Article 318).
Even if only the land is recorded as mortgaged, where the land user is also the owner of the house, the property enforced includes the house, unless otherwise agreed (Clause 1, Article 325).
h2
2. The mortgage contract: notarisation and registration
ul
A contract mortgaging a land use right, or a land use right together with assets attached to the land, must be notarised or authenticated (Point a, Clause 3, Article 27 of the Land Law 2024).
The contract takes effect from the time it is concluded, unless otherwise agreed or provided by law; a mortgage becomes effective against third parties from the time of registration (Article 319).
The mortgagee carries out the mortgage registration as prescribed (Clause 4, Article 323).
h2
3. What can the borrower still do with the house?
p
Under Article 321, the mortgagor may:
ul
Exploit the utility of the house and land and enjoy the fruits and profits from it (living in it, doing business), unless the fruits are also mortgaged property by agreement.
Invest to increase the value of the asset (for example, repairing or upgrading the house).
Lease or lend it, but must inform the tenant that the house is mortgaged and inform the bank.
Sell or gift the mortgaged house and land only with the mortgagee's consent or as provided by law.
Get the title documents back once the debt has been fully repaid.
h2
4. Obligations of the mortgagor
p

Under Article 320, the mortgagor must preserve and maintain the asset; when it is damaged, repair it or replace it with an equivalent asset within a reasonable time (unless otherwise agreed); provide information on the actual condition of the asset; notify the bank of any third-party rights over the asset (if any); and must not sell, substitute, exchange or gift the mortgaged asset other than in permitted cases.
p
The bank has the right to inspect the asset directly but must not obstruct its use and exploitation (Article 323).
h2
5. When does the bank enforce against the house and land?
p

The secured asset is enforced when the borrower fails to repay when due or repays improperly; when early repayment is required because of a breach of obligations; or in other cases agreed or provided by law (Article 299).
ul
Before enforcement, the bank must give written notice within a reasonable period; if it fails to do so and causes loss, it must pay compensation (Article 300).

The method of enforcement is agreed by the parties: public auction, sale by the bank itself, taking the asset itself in place of the obligation, or another method; absent agreement, the asset is sold by public auction unless the law provides otherwise (Article 303).

From the sale proceeds, after deducting the costs of preserving, seizing and enforcing the asset: if the proceeds are greater than the debt, the difference must be returned to the borrower; if they are smaller, the borrower must still pay the shortfall (Article 307).
When the bank enforces the asset, it also declares and pays personal income tax on the borrower's behalf before settling the debt (Point c, Clause 6, Article 57 of Decree 253/2026/ND-CP).
h2
6. Points to note before signing
ol
Read carefully the terms on the method of enforcement and the cases in which early repayment can be demanded.
Where the house and land are the joint property of spouses or a family, the signatures of all co-owners are needed.
To sell a mortgaged house you need the bank's consent; usually the loan is repaid to release the mortgage before, or at the same time as, the sale.
Borrow only what you can repay monthly even if interest rates rise; keep a reserve fund covering several months of repayments.
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal texts. Mortgage registration procedures and the banking sector's own regulations are not yet in our library. The Land Law 2024 is currently partially no longer in force. Read the credit contract and the mortgage contract carefully and ask the bank before signing.
